title: Fine structure constant: CODATA comparison
html:
The electromagnetic coupling (EM coupling projection) predicts \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} directly from the substrate parameter q. It requires zero free parameters.

Bare formula.

  \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}^{-1}(q)
  = 
  q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q
  = 136.823.

The force-carrier generators T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} (force identification) dictate the crossing numbers 9 and 10. The Descartes substrate parameter fixes the q-integers.

Derived correction. The leading correction to the bare formula is additive. It derives from the photon infrared zero-mode on Bring's surface (photon IR zero-mode):

  \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}^{-1}(q) = q \cdot [9]_q \cdot [10]_q + \frac{2}{3\pi},
  \qquad \frac{2}{3\pi} = \frac{b_1(M_{\mathrm{Bring}})}{\mathrm{Area}(M_{\mathrm{Bring}})}
  = \frac{2g}{4\pi(g-1)}\Big|_{g=4}.

The genus-4 topology fixes b_1 = 2g = 8 and the Gauss–Bonnet area. The corrected value is 137.0354. This leaves a -4.2\;\mathrm{ppm} residual against the CODATA value of 137.035999. This additive correction improves the bare form by a factor of 370.

Self-energy correction. The remaining -4.2\;\mathrm{ppm} is a Schwinger-type self-energy effect, and its coefficient is not an unknown: it is H = [2]_q/(8\pi), whose denominator 8\pi = \pi\,b_1 is fixed by the same genus-4 topology as the zero mode. Because [2]_q/2 = 1.00545 at the substrate value, H is the q-deformation of the classical Schwinger coefficient 1/(4\pi), exceeding it by 0.545\%. Retaining it, together with the cubic factor (1 - h^2\alpha) where h = q - q^{-1} is the Hecke structure constant, gives

  \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}^{-1}(q)
  = q\,[9]_q\,[10]_q + \frac{2}{3\pi} + \alpha H (1 - h^2 \alpha) + \Delta_2 .

Since \alpha stands on both sides, this is solved as a fixed point rather than evaluated as a series. The result is 137.035999127, a residual of +0.313 parts per billion — roughly 2.1 times the CODATA uncertainty, and about 13{,}600 times closer than the additive form quoted above.

What remains genuinely open is \Delta_2, the archimedean two-loop term: a weight-three, \zeta(3)-type Bloch-group normalisation in B_3(\mathbb{C}) over the ideal hyperbolic tetrahedra of Bring's surface (α_EM derivation open problems). It is distinct from the weight-one -h^2H\alpha^2 term already carried in the form. The whole chain is also conditional on three unproved classes, so none of this is a closed derivation; what has changed is only that the self-energy coefficient itself is no longer among the missing pieces.

Numerical comparison. See Table 1.

Inversion: q from \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}. Fixing \alpha^{-1} at the CODATA value and solving for q yields

  q_\alpha = 1.10997858247973714 .

The inversion must be run on the full form above; inverting the additive form alone returns 1.11023, which is 226\;\mathrm{ppm} away and reflects the missing self-energy term rather than any property of the substrate.

Against the substrate parameter q_0 = 1.109978582751\ldots pinned on the proton ratio, q_\alpha sits 0.245 parts per billion away; against the muon pin it sits 11.8 ppb away. The electromagnetic sector therefore agrees with the proton anchor to sub-ppb and identifies the muon as the outlier, which is the same muon–proton substrate tension that appears in the mass sector, seen here in a third independent observable (half-life as q-probe). The agreement is a genuine cross-check rather than a fit: no coefficient was adjusted, only q solved for.

Sensitivity. The coupling depends steeply on q:

  \frac{\partial \ln \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}}{\partial \ln q}
  =  -1 - 
  \frac{9  q^9 [10]_q + 10  q^{10} [9]_q}
       {[9]_q [10]_q (q - q^{-1})}.

At q = q_0, this derivative is approximately -20. A 1\% shift in q drives a \sim 20\% shift in \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}. The empirical agreement bounds q around q_0.

Comparison. See Table 2.

The substrate parameter q_0 is overdetermined: the electromagnetic coupling, the mass ratios and the decay rates each determine it independently. They do not converge on an identical value, and the residual spread is informative rather than noise. The electromagnetic and proton-mass determinations agree to sub-ppb, while the muon ratio sits some 11.5 ppb away — a discrepancy far larger than either determination's own precision, and the reason the experimental pin is taken on the proton.
